title: Token-Forcing Audit: Which Specific Compliant Prefixes Are Most Dangerous?

original_idea.body: Token-Forcing Audit. Problem: produce a ranked catalogue of which compliant prefix phrases yield the highest jailbreak rates per model. Direction: curate ~30 candidate compliant prefixes, prefill each on a fixed harmful set, rank by StrongReject-scored ASR per open model, test whether dangerous prefixes are shared across models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a ranked dangerous-prefix dictionary is an actionable defensive artifact grounded in the shallow-alignment exploit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prefill ~30 prefixes + StrongReject scoring on open models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped ranking experiment with clear deliverable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-model prefilling audit producing a transferable artifact.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only prefilling on a harmful set, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Prefilling attacks and shallow alignment are published; a per-prefix ranking is incremental.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Prefilling exploits are published; a ranked-prefix catalogue is an incremental extension.
